basics.name: Santiago Espinosa Mooser
basics.label: Quantitative Technologist at QRT
basics.summary: I'm a Quantitative Technologist at QRT (Qube Research & Technologies) in Hong Kong, doing platform work for quantitative research and trading. Before that I was a Senior DevSecOps Engineer at Hex Trust (digital-asset custody), and I still build things on the side: market-microstructure benchmarks in Rust, trading-competition bots, and the self-hosted Kubernetes lab I run at home. I have a Computer Science degree from HKU with a theory focus (algorithms, game theory, cryptography), and I like being the least knowledgeable person in the room. If any of this is interesting, feel free to reach out by email.

work.name: Hex Trust
work.description: Hex Trust is a fully-licensed provider of bank-grade custody for digital assets with a focus on security and compliance.
work.summary: Rejoined Hex Trust full-time as the in-house DevSecOps engineer, progressing from intern to L13 (Senior) across my time at the company. Focused on hardening cloud workloads and improving the company's technical security posture.
highlights: Designed and implemented the CI/CD pipeline to build, sign, deploy, and debug distroless containers; coordinated the developer teams' migration and ran internal talks on working with them.

Deployed and managed the company's Privileged Access Management platform (Teleport) across Kubernetes clusters, RDS databases, web applications, and Linux servers using Terragrunt, Helm, and AWS EKS, providing auditable real-time access to production.
Designed and deployed RBAC roles for AWS, Kubernetes, databases, and Linux servers, making production access auditable and maintainable.

Integrated a CSPM platform across cloud and on-prem servers and implemented custom Kubernetes and cloud alerting; deployed the monitoring stack with Helm, CloudFormation, and ArgoCD across multiple clouds.
Organized, launched, and ran the company's private bug-bounty program; coordinated fixes and used the findings to steer security priorities.
Automated security processes in Python, Go, and Bash — for example, MDM device whitelisting.

Acted as main contact for security incidents: led the response, wrote incident reports, and presented results to the CTO; served as internal security counsel for developers, including cryptography questions.

work.name: Hex Trust
work.description: Hex Trust is a fully-licensed provider of bank-grade custody for digital assets with a focus on security and compliance.
work.summary: Head-hunted into an internship, then continued part-time through my final year of studies. Focused on shifting security left and improving security reporting across the company.
highlights: Designed, implemented, and maintained the company's first DevSecOps pipeline, preventing vulnerable code, secrets, and dependencies from reaching production with Snyk, tfsec, Clair, TruffleHog, and other SAST tools, adapted to the company's branching strategy.
Led the Snyk vulnerability-management rollout, cutting active, potentially exploitable vulnerabilities by 20% in the first month.
Deployed and maintained a next-gen WAF (Signal Sciences) protecting against the OWASP Top 10, web CVEs, and enumeration attacks, with the ruleset managed through Terraform.
Automated YubiKey provisioning, reducing per-key setup from ~45 minutes to under 1 minute (scripts open-sourced on my GitHub), and led the adoption of YubiKeys for company-wide code signing.
Investigated critical security incidents through SIEM and WAF log analysis and reported recommendations to the Head of Cybersecurity.

Managed the company's on-prem servers and VMs, deploying and maintaining internal services including GitLab, Bookstack, Samba, Elasticsearch, and a Microsoft domain controller.

projects.name: mmap-sync HFT benchmark
projects.description: Benchmarked Cloudflare's mmap-sync IPC library (Rust) under HFT-style workloads: 192-byte bid/ask structs, Hawkes-distributed bursty writes, and 12 concurrent readers on isolated cores, measured with Criterion.rs on a tuned Ryzen 7 5800X3D. Reads were stable at ~31 µs, but writes spiked to 14 ms (+233%) in 16% of samples — concluding mmap-sync is unsuitable for latency-critical write paths.

projects.name: IMC Prosperity 2024
projects.description: Trading competition (team Quant Crusaders): finished #729 of 10,000+ teams, top 15 in Hong Kong. Implemented RSI momentum, linear-regression prediction, pair-trading, and market-making strategies for bonds, ETFs, stocks, and options in Python across 3 of 5 rounds; code and analysis notebooks are public.

projects.name: Jane Street Electronic Trading Challenge 2022
projects.description: Real-time PvP trading challenge: wrote a live trading bot competing against other participants on a simulated exchange trading bonds, ETFs, and stocks. Finished #4 of 30 participants.

projects.name: Crypto arbitrage simulator
projects.description: Crypto arbitrage simulator in Python (ccxt): polls order books from multiple exchanges, detects cross-exchange spread opportunities, and simulates fills net of per-exchange taker fees. Built to learn exchange microstructure — including why naive spread arbitrage rarely survives fees and latency.

projects.name: Self-hosted Kubernetes homelab
